Estimate the Dynamic Nelson-Siegel Model in One Step

Source: R/dns-kalman.R
estimate_dns_state_space.Rd

Fits the DNS model to a panel of yield curves by maximum likelihood, with the factors treated as an unobserved state and filtered out of the yields, rather than fitted curve by curve and then modelled. This is the one-step state-space approach of Diebold, Rudebusch and Aruoba (2006), as against the two-step approach of Diebold and Li (2006) that fit_dns_model and estimate_dns_dynamics implement between them.

Usage

estimate_dns_state_space(
  yield_data,
  n_days = NULL,
  sampling = c("monthly", "all"),
  lambda = NULL,
  measurement = c("per_maturity", "common"),
  dt = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  maxit = 500L,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

yield_data

Data frame. Yield curve panel with a Date column and one column per maturity, named by maturity in years – the same shape fit_dns_model takes.

n_days

Integer or NULL. Use only the most recent n_days dates. NULL (the default) uses all of them.

sampling

Character. "monthly" (the default) keeps the last observation in each calendar month, the frequency this model is usually estimated at; "all" uses every date.

lambda

Numeric or NULL. NULL (the default) estimates lambda jointly with the dynamics. A number holds it fixed, which is faster.

measurement

Character. "per_maturity" (the default) gives each maturity its own measurement error variance, as in Diebold, Rudebusch and Aruoba; "common" estimates a single variance for all maturities, which is better determined on short panels.

dt

Numeric or NULL. Time step between observations, in years. NULL (the default) infers it from the median spacing of the dates used.

start

List or NULL. Optional starting values, with any of the elements kappa, theta, sigma, correlation, lambda, measurement_sd. NULL (the default) starts from the two-step estimates, which are also reported on the result.

maxit

Integer. Maximum optimiser iterations. Default 500.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, report the log-likelihood as it improves.

Value

A list with class "dns_state_space". Its beta1/beta2/beta3, correlation and lambda elements are shaped so that dns_dynamics_to_sim_params accepts it directly:

  • beta1, beta2, beta3: each a list of kappa, theta and sigma, plus the implied half_life

  • correlation: the 3-by-3 shock correlation matrix

  • lambda: the decay parameter, estimated or as supplied

  • factors: data frame of smoothed factors by date, directly comparable with the parameters frame fit_dns_model() returns

  • filtered: the filtered factors, using only data up to each date

  • measurement_sd: fitted measurement error per maturity, in the units of the input yields

  • logLik, n_params, aic, bic: fit and its cost in parameters

  • fitted, residuals: fitted yields from the smoothed factors, and observed minus fitted

  • rmse: root mean squared measurement residual

  • kappa_matrix, theta_vector, eigenvalues, system_stability: as estimate_dns_dynamics reports them

  • two_step: the two-step estimates used as starting values

  • convergence, message: from optim

  • dt, sampling, structure, n_dates, maturities

Details

The model is $$y_t = \Lambda(\lambda) f_t + e_t, \quad e_t \sim N(0, H)$$ $$f_t = \theta + A (f_{t-1} - \theta) + \eta_t, \quad \eta_t \sim N(0, Q)$$ with \(\Lambda\) the Nelson-Siegel loadings and \(H\) diagonal. \(A\) and \(Q\) are the transition law of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck system the rest of the package simulates: $$A_{ii} = e^{-\kappa_i \Delta t}$$ $$Q_{ij} = \rho_{ij} \sigma_i \sigma_j (1 - e^{-(\kappa_i+\kappa_j)\Delta t}) / (\kappa_i + \kappa_j)$$

\(A\) and \(Q\) are therefore functions of \(\kappa\), \(\sigma\) and \(\rho\) rather than free parameters. This has three consequences. \(Q\) is a covariance matrix at every trial point. \(\kappa > 0\) makes the system stationary, so the filter has a proper initial covariance. And the result is in the parameters dns_dynamics_to_sim_params and simulate_dns_factors accept, so a fit can be simulated forward without conversion. The cost is that cross-factor terms cannot be represented.

One step against two. The two-step estimator uses the fitted betas as data. They are estimates carrying sampling error, and using them as observed in a time-series regression biases mean reversion upward, the errors-in-variables direction. Filtering the factors propagates that uncertainty into the likelihood and estimates \(\lambda\) jointly with the dynamics. The costs are run time, needing the whole panel at once, and a harder numerical problem: a dozen or more parameters in one optimisation rather than a sequence of independent three-parameter fits.

Limitations. The factor system is diagonal: each factor reverts to its own mean at its own speed, with contemporaneously correlated shocks. A full mean-reversion matrix is not supported. Supporting it would require a matrix exponential for \(A\) and a Sylvester solve for \(Q\), and dns_dynamics_to_sim_params discards cross terms, so the result could not be simulated by the rest of the package. Use estimate_dns_dynamics(structure = "full") on two-step betas for the cross terms.

Missing yields shrink the measurement equation for that date rather than dropping the date, so a curve missing one maturity still contributes its other maturities and leaves no gap in the series.

Precision of the estimates. The parameters divide into two groups. Simulating from a known DNS state space with monthly data and ten maturities, then re-estimating, gives these percentage errors:

  • \(\lambda\): within 1 percent at 20, 40 and 100 years of data.

  • \(\sigma\): within 5 percent at all three lengths.

  • measurement standard deviation: within 1 percent at all three.

  • \(\kappa\) for the level factor: 167 percent too high at 20 years, 77 percent at 40, 58 percent at 100.

  • \(\theta\) for the slope factor: 54 percent low at 20 years, 66 percent high at 40, 2 percent low at 100.

\(\lambda\), the shock volatilities and the measurement error are recovered precisely at realistic sample lengths, and the smoothed factors correlate above 0.99 with the simulated ones. The mean reversion speeds and long-run means are not. \(\kappa\) carries an upward bias that decays as the sample lengthens, and \(\theta\) has a standard error of the same order as its own value, because a factor with a multi-year half-life supplies few independent observations about its long-run mean however finely it is sampled.

The errors shrink toward zero as the sample grows, so this reflects the difficulty of estimating mean reversion rather than an error in the implementation, and it applies to the two-step route as well. Treat \(\kappa\) and \(\theta\) as approximate.

References

Diebold, F.X., Rudebusch, G.D. and Aruoba, S.B. (2006). The macroeconomy and the yield curve: a dynamic latent factor approach. Journal of Econometrics 131, 309-338.

Diebold, F.X. and Li, C. (2006). Forecasting the term structure of government bond yields. Journal of Econometrics 130, 337-364.

See also

fit_dns_model and estimate_dns_dynamics for the two-step route, dns_dynamics_to_sim_params to simulate a fit forward.

Examples

# Maximising the likelihood takes a few seconds, so the example is not run
# during checks. The run time is dominated by the number of optimiser
# iterations rather than by the size of the panel.
# \donttest{
# Two years of the bundled panel, thinned to month-ends. lambda is held
# fixed here; pass lambda = NULL to estimate it jointly with the dynamics.
# n_days counts rows of the input, which is daily, so 500 trading days
# leaves 24 month-ends to filter.
fit <- estimate_dns_state_space(treasury_yields, n_days = 500,
                                lambda = ns_lambda(3.5),
                                measurement = "common")
fit
#> DNS one-step state-space fit (Kalman filter, maximum likelihood)
#>   estimated on     2023-01-31 to 2024-12-31
#>   sampling         monthly (dt = 1/11.8), 24 dates, 11 maturities
#>   lambda           0.5124 fixed (hump at 3.50 years)
#> 
#>                 kappa   theta  sigma  half_life_y
#> level (b1)     0.0000  0.0436 0.0000 1.819697e+09
#> slope (b2)     0.7682  0.0064 0.0066 9.023000e-01
#> curvature (b3) 7.9965 -0.0200 0.0535 8.670000e-02
#> 
#>   measurement sd   20.84 bp median across maturities
#>   fit              19.39 bp rmse
#>   logLik           1209.63 on 13 parameters (AIC -2393.3, BIC -2346.8)
#>   stable           TRUE
#>   $two_step holds the two-step estimates used as starting values

# The shock correlation, the measurement error by maturity, and the
# two-step estimates alongside the one-step ones
summary(fit)
#> DNS one-step state-space fit (Kalman filter, maximum likelihood)
